practiceReport.beatComment: Green sustained a back injury during San Francisco's win versus the Raiders in Week 9, and now his availability for Week 10 is in question. His activity at practice will be worth monitoring over the course of the week, and the 49ers' first official injury report of the week Wednesday should provide further insight into his status.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nate Hobbs
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 8 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hobbs had his practice window opened Wednesday and logged three limited practices before initially being deemed questionable to face the Raiders on Sunday. Since he wasn't activated Saturday, the veteran cornerback will have to wait at least another week to return to action. Hobbs' next chance to do so is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Dallas.

irAndReserveTracker.name: C.J. West
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The 49ers expect WR Deebo Samuel and DT CJ West to be back at practice on Wednesday, coach Kyle Shanahan said. West was placed on injured reserve in late September due to an undisclosed injury but is now nearing his return. Once the practice window is officially opened, San Francisco will have 21 days to activate the 2025 fourth-round pick, or else he'll be forced to stay on injured reserve for the remainder of the campaign.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Christian Kirk
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Kirk made his season debut in San Francisco's last game in Week 7 in Atlanta, going without a target on a 30 percent snap share. After a Week 8 bye, he showed up on the initial Week 9 practice report Wednesday as limited due to a knee injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed to be to the wide receiver's meniscus Friday, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com. Shanahan also relayed that Robinson may need surgery, but at the very least he'll miss the team's next four contests.

irAndReserveTracker.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Sam Okuayinonu
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday he hopes Okuayinonu can return near the end of the regular season, but it is unclear quite how long the recovery process will take. Okuayinonu previously had a plate in his foot, and the break occurred when it was stepped on during practice.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Austen Pleasants
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Pleasants sustained a knee injury during the 49ers' preseason game against the Chargers on Aug. 20. The injury is severe enough for 29-year-old offensive tackle to open the year on IR, meaning he'll be forced to miss at least the first four games of the regular season.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Isaac Guerendo
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Guerendo spent all of training camp on the active/PUP list and is seemingly not ready to take the field, so he will remain on PUP and will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. As such, Kaelon Black and Jordan James will open as the top two options behind starter Christian McCaffrey (undisclosed).

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Martin
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Martin opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during training camp in August. Shanahan said Martin is "getting close" to returning to practice, and if he's cleared for field work this week, his participation level will shed light on whether he'll play in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19. The 2025 third-rounder logged 11 tackles (eight solo) and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games during his rookie campaign, which he finished on injured reserve due to a concussion.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Brandon Aiyuk
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Two-week NFL roster exemption following reinstatement
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to either add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Alfred Collins
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: This move was anticipated, as Collins is set to miss the entire 2026 campaign as a result of tearing his patellar tendon during practice Tuesday. Osa Odighizuwa, CJ West and Gracen Halton should get plenty of reps at defensive tackle with Collins and Sam Okuayinonu (foot) sidelined.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Andrew Farmer II
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Farmer was not picked up by another squad after the 49ers waived him with an injury designation earlier in the week, and now he'll be required to stay on the team's IR list for the year unless he negotiates an injury settlement. He last played regular-season snaps in 2023 with the Chargers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Darrick Forrest
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: It's not clear what kind of injury Forrest is dealing with, but he's now on track to spend the entire 2026 season on IR unless he negotiates an injury settlement with the 49ers. His absence could open up more opportunities for rookie undrafted free agents Jalen Stroman and Larry Worth.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Gracen Halton
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jake Tonges
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The team placed Tonges on injured reserve earlier Wednesday, and now it's official that he will miss the rest of the season. Tonges suffered an MCL tear in the season opener against the Rams. Jack Stoll was signed to the practice squad to add depth, and Luke Farrell now projects to be the second tight end behind George Kittle.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mikail Kamara
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Placed on Injured Reserve (Knee) on Aug 3, 2026; ineligible to return in 2026 under NFL CBA rules.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Zakelj
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The nature of Zakelj's injury is unclear, as is when he exactly picked up the injury. However, by being placed on IR without a designation to return, the 2022 sixth-rounder will be forced to miss the entire upcoming season unless he reached an injury settlement with San Francisco.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ricky Pearsall
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The procedure typically carries a wide-ranging recovery timeline of 6-to-12 months, so while Pearsall will be ruled out for the season, it's not clear if he'll be available for the start of the 49ers' offseason program next spring or the start of training camp next summer. The wideout will wind up having played in just 20 of a possible 51 regular-season contests and one of two playoff games through his first three NFL campaigns, missing time as a rookie while recovering from a gunshot wound to the chest before being hampered by the PCL injury off and on in 2025. He'll turn 27 in September and will be entering the final season of his rookie contract in 2027.
